stem: A model carries an enforced contract and is materialized as `incremental`. The platform engineer needs the model to keep building successfully after a new column is added upstream, without breaking the contract. Which `on_schema_change` setting keeps this model compliant, and why?

option_texts.A: No on_schema_change setting is needed, because an enforced contract alone covers this case
option_texts.B: `ignore` (the default), because an enforced contract does not change how schema drift is handled
option_texts.C: `on_schema_change: sync_all_columns`, because it is the most permissive option and contracts always prefer permissive settings
option_texts.D: `append_new_columns`, because that is one of only two on_schema_change settings dbt allows for this materialization

drill_answer_short: Contracted incremental models support only append_new_columns or fail for on_schema_change
decision_hinge: These places support model contracts: incremental, with on_schema_change: append_new_columns or on_schema_change: fail.

plausible_options.C: needs the model to keep building successfully after a new column is added upstream

eliminated_by.A: A model carries an enforced contract and is materialized as `incremental`

B.signal: needs the model to keep building successfully after a new column is added upstream
B.requires_fact: An incremental model supports model contracts only with on_schema_change set to append_new_columns or fail.

distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated — contracted incremental models still require one of the two supported settings
distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated — dbt does not consider contracts and schema-change handling independent of each other
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling — sync_all_columns is a real setting, but it is not one of the two settings contracts support

stem: A team runs `dbt run --full-refresh --select stg_events`. `stg_events` is materialized as incremental and its SQL is wrapped in an `is_incremental()` block that filters for new rows. The team must predict exactly what happens during this invocation. Which TWO statements are correct?

option_texts.A: `is_incremental()` evaluates to `False` for this run, because the full-refresh flag is set
option_texts.B: dbt drops the existing target table before rebuilding it for all time
option_texts.C: dbt merges new rows into the existing table without dropping it, since `--full-refresh` only changes filtering, not table structure
option_texts.D: `is_incremental()` still evaluates to `True`, because the model is still configured with `materialized='incremental'`, regardless of the full-refresh flag

drill_answer_short: --full-refresh makes is_incremental() return False and drops the table before rebuilding it
decision_hinge: The is_incremental() macro will return True only if the full-refresh flag is not passed, among other conditions. The --full-refresh flag will cause dbt to drop the existing target table in the database before rebuilding it for all-time.

plausible_options.D: its SQL is wrapped in an `is_incremental()` block that filters for new rows

C.requires_fact: The --full-refresh flag will cause dbt to drop the existing target table in the database before rebuilding it for all-time.

distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated — --full-refresh does drop and rebuild the table, not merely re-filter it
distractor_traps.D: T8: scope error — one condition being true does not make is_incremental() return True; all of its conditions must hold

stem: A snapshot `scd_raw_listings` is configured with `strategy: timestamp`, `updated_at: updated_at`. A developer accidentally also adds `check_cols: ['name', 'price']` to the same snapshot config. What happens when the snapshot next runs?

option_texts.A: dbt raises a compilation error, because `check_cols` and `strategy: timestamp` cannot both be present
option_texts.B: dbt ignores `check_cols`; the snapshot keeps detecting changes using `updated_at` under the `timestamp` strategy
option_texts.C: dbt switches the snapshot to the `check` strategy automatically, since `check_cols` was provided
option_texts.D: dbt uses both `updated_at` and `check_cols` together, detecting a change whenever either one differs

drill_answer_short: check_cols only applies to the check strategy; a timestamp-strategy snapshot keeps using updated_at
decision_hinge: check_cols: if using the check strategy, then the columns to check; only needed if using the check strategy. updated_at: a column that indicates when each record was last updated, used in the timestamp strategy; only needed if using the timestamp strategy.

plausible_options.D: A developer accidentally also adds `check_cols: ['name', 'price']` to the same snapshot config

C.requires_fact: check_cols is only needed if using the check strategy, and updated_at is only needed if using the timestamp strategy; dbt does not switch strategies based on which fields are present.

distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated — dbt does not reject this configuration at compile time
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated — the configured strategy does not change based on which extra fields are present
distractor_traps.D: T3: confusable sibling — treats the two single-strategy fields as if they combine, when each belongs to a different strategy

stem: A project needs a SQL statement to run once, at the start of `dbt build`, before any individual model is built -- not before or after each model -- and an engineer must choose the correct hook type for this. Which hook fits, and why?

option_texts.A: `post-hook`, because it executes after a model, seed, or snapshot is built
option_texts.B: `pre-hook`, because it executes before a model is built
option_texts.C: `on-run-start`, because it executes once at the start of commands like `dbt build`, `dbt run`, and `dbt test`
option_texts.D: `on-run-end`, because it executes once per invocation, at the end

drill_answer_short: on-run-start executes once at the start of commands such as dbt build, not per model
decision_hinge: on-run-start is executed at the start of dbt build, dbt compile, dbt docs generate, dbt run, dbt seed, dbt snapshot, or dbt test. pre-hook is executed before a model, seed, or snapshot is built. post-hook is executed after a model, seed or snapshot is built.

plausible_options.B: before any individual model is built

eliminated_by.A: not before or after each model

D.signal: needs a SQL statement to run once, at the start of `dbt build`
D.requires_fact: on-run-start is executed at the start of a command; on-run-end is executed at the end.

distractor_traps.A: T4: breaks a stated requirement — post-hook runs after, not before, and still runs per resource
distractor_traps.B: T8: scope error — pre-hook runs once per model, seed, or snapshot, not once for the whole invocation
distractor_traps.D: T8: scope error — on-run-end fires once, but at the end, not the start
